entries.title: Iran says US reply to Hormuz plan ‘unconvincing’; Trump confirms strikes
entries.summary: Indirect talks continue as Trump says US military struck an Iranian anti-aircraft facility on Tuesday.
entries.content:
Indirect talks continue as Trump says US military struck an Iranian anti-aircraft facility on Tuesday.

Iran has called the US response to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz “unconvincing” as US President Donald Trump confirmed launching strikes on an Iranian island near the strategic waterway.

The developments on Tuesday came as Qatar stepped up diplomatic efforts to avert a renewed war between the US and Iran and as another oil tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.

The indirect talks centre on an Iranian proposal to reopen the waterway over two days, if the US meets Tehran’s seven demands, including the lifting of sanctions and ending a US naval blockade.

Despite reports of progress in recent days, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said on Tuesday that Washington’s response had fallen short.

“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing, and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them,” he wrote on X.

“Only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”

His post came after Majed al-Ansari, a spokesperson for Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that talks were continuing and that both sides “remain committed to the negotiation process”.

He said Qatar was facilitating the “real-time exchange of proposals between” the US and Iran.

Attack on Qeshm Island

In Washington, DC, Trump confirmed the US had struck Iran early on Tuesday, telling Fox News that the strikes had targeted an anti-aircraft facility.

He described the operation as a “minor attack” and said it “wasn’t war”.

“They built an anti-aircraft facility. It took them about two months. We watched it get built. As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night,” he said.

Iranian media said the strikes hit Qeshm Island in the Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier in the day, US officials told US media that the strikes had been “defensive” and followed Iranian fire at an American aircraft.

The strikes came as US media, citing US officials, reported that Central Command had prepared plans for strikes that could begin as early as Wednesday, after the midterm elections, when three American aircraft carriers would be in the region.

The crucial elections could cost Trump’s Republicans control of both the House and the Senate, and fears have grown that Trump could carry out a threatened attack on Iran once the vote is over.

US media have previously reported that the planned campaign would be short and intense.

Trump meanwhile repeated warnings of further military action on Tuesday, saying, “I’m not looking to … kill lots of people” and “If we have to, we’ll have to.”

In an earlier interview with the Financial Times, he suggested he was content with the state of the stand-off with Iran. “We seem to be getting everything we want,” the paper quoted him as saying in a six-minute telephone interview.

Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, meanwhile ordered the military at the weekend to respond to any threat immediately and without geographical limits, and to update its list of targets.

Iranian officials have suggested that European countries and undersea cables in the Gulf could be targeted.

Tanker struck in Hormuz

As officials weighed the possibility of escalation, commercial shipping came under further attack.

The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that two unidentified projectiles struck a tanker’s engine room about 14 nautical miles (26km) northeast of Oman’s coastal village of Limah on Tuesday. No casualties were reported.

Separately, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed four tankers had struck mines and caught fire after switching off navigation and identification systems and using what it described as unauthorised routes through Hormuz, and said its forces had seized two other vessels.

That account could not be independently verified or linked to the incident reported by UKMTO.

The IRGC also claimed it had destroyed two US LUCAS attack drones over Bandar Khamir, according to Iranian state broadcaster Pars Today.

John Mearsheimer, a US political scientist, questioned whether another short bombing campaign could achieve Washington’s objectives, warning that Iranian retaliation could draw the US into a longer confrontation.

“If the 40-day bombing campaign didn’t work, how is the three-day bombing campaign going to work?” he asked in a video commentary, referring to the initial US-Israeli air campaign and proposals for a shorter renewed offensive.

He argued that an Iranian response could prompt further US escalation, increasing the damage to the global economy.

entries.title: Kansas elects first Democratic senator in almost a century
entries.summary: Adam Hamilton beat Republican Roger Marshall in a highly competitive race.
entries.content:
Adam Hamilton beat out Republican Roger Marshall in a highly competitive race.

Democrat Adam Hamilton has become the first member of his party to win a Kansas Senate seat in almost a century after beating incumbent Republican Roger Marshall, according to Associated Press news agency projections.

The race was considered consequential to control of the US Senate.

The highly competitive contest between Hamilton, a Methodist pastor, and Marshall stunned political observers given the state’s long history of Republican wins. A Democrat has not won a Senate seat in Kansas since 1932.

The founder of the largest United Methodist church in the country, Hamilton campaigned as a man of faith while pushing core Democratic positions on affordability. Like other rural states, Kansas has seen its agricultural and transportation industries hit by record-high diesel and fuel prices.

“We’re always told to not talk about politics or religion but this is one time we’re trying to save our democracy. The next two years are a pivotal time for our country,” Hamilton said on Monday.

Marshall is a staunch supporter of US President Donald Trump, who campaigned for the Republican candidate.

Marshall pushed Trump’s agenda during the campaign and pledged to expand rural healthcare, despite voting for Trump’s funding cuts, and to support agriculture. A physician, he has stirred controversy by supporting Trump’s Make America Healthy Again policies, which critics say undermine public health, and by opposing mask mandates during the pandemic.

Marshall’s campaign was also dogged by a New York Times report that he had sued about 700 of his former patients for medical debt during his years as a doctor, which Hamilton’s campaign used in attack ads.

The Associated Press reported that the $110m race was the most expensive in the state’s history.

entries.title: Democratic Party flips US Senate in 2026 midterm elections
entries.summary: The outcome is widely seen as a rebuke to Trump's Republican Party which took control of the upper chamber in 2024 race.
entries.content:
The outcome is widely seen as a rebuke to Trump’s Republican Party, which took control of the upper chamber in the 2024 election.

The Democratic Party has regained control of upper chamber of the United States Congress in the 2026 midterm elections.

On Tuesday night, the Senate was called in the left-wing party’s favour, marking a dramatic shift in legislative power.

Democrats needed to gain four seats in the upper chamber of Congress to wrest control from the Republicans.

Some of those gains were dramatic. In South Carolina, for instance, Democratic doctor Annie Andrews nabbed a seat held by Republican Darline Graham, the sister of the late longtime Senator Lindsey Graham. The last time a Democrat won a Senate seat in the state was 1998.

Neighbouring North Carolina saw a similar Senate flip, with Democrat Roy Cooper, a former governor, beating his Republican rival Michael Whatley.

In deep-red Texas, meanwhile, Democrat seminarian James Talarico delivered an upset against state Attorney General Ken Paxton. The last time a Democrat won a statewide election in Texas was 1994.

Democrat Sherrod Brown also defeated incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted in Ohio, flipping that seat as well. And in Kansas, Adam Hamilton, the Democratic pastor of a mega-church, beat another sitting senator, Republican Roger Marshall.

Currently, in the outgoing 119th Congress, Republicans have a 53-person majority in the 100-seat chamber. The Democrats have a 45-member minority, with two independents in their caucus.

But with Tuesday’s results, the Senate majority will shift hands.

The outcome is also slated to end the Republican “trifecta”, achieved during the 2024 election, which saw the right-wing party win leadership over three major bodies of power in Washington, DC: the Senate, the House of Representatives and the presidency.

The Senate was projected to be harder to flip than the House in Tuesday’s midterm elections, given the smaller number of seats on the ballot.

Senate terms last six years, unlike the two-year terms given to elected members in the House of Representatives. And elections for senators are staggered, meaning that only a third of all Senate seats will be voted upon at at time.

This midterm election cycle saw 35 Senate races unfold: 33 regular elections, and two special elections in Ohio and Florida. Those two states were left with Senate vacancies when Vice President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio joined President Donald Trump’s second administration in 2025.

At least seven Senate races on Tuesday were considered key toss-ups. They included contests in Alaska, Iowa, Kansas, Maine, Ohio, Texas and Michigan.

States like Texas and Kansas, however, rarely fall within the toss-up category, as they are considered right-wing strongholds. The last time a Democratic senator was elected in Kansas was 1932.

“How did this happen? How did a Democrat win in Kansas, a deeply red state, for the first time in nearly a century, especially in a state where only 25 percent of the people are Democrats?” Kansas’s Senator-elect Hamilton said in his victory speech.

“First of all, I think the people in Kansas — Republicans, independents and Democrats — were saying what’s happening in Washington is not OK.”

The Democratic Party also successfully defended several seats, including in Jon Ossoff’s race in the swing state of Georgia. Mark Warner, a 17-year veteran of the Senate, also retained his position representing Virginia, scoring a fourth term with Tuesday’s victory.

More updates to come…

entries.title: Democrat Amy Acton beats Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in Ohio governor’s race
entries.summary: Acton is the first Democrat to become governor of Ohio since 2006.
entries.content:
Acton is the first Democrat to become governor of Ohio since 2006.

Democrat Amy Acton has been elected as the US state of Ohio’s next governor, delivering a stunning defeat to Republican Vivek Ramaswamy in a race that captured headlines across the country.

Acton, a physician who served as outgoing Republican Governor Mike DeWine’s top health official, faced countless attacks over her response to the Covid-19 pandemic. Spending in the hotly contested race topped an unprecedented $100m.

In the final weeks of the bitter campaign, a controversial television ad featuring her estranged mother sparked fierce backlash against Ramaswamy, who claimed responsibility for it and refused to take it down off the airwaves.

In the ad, Acton’s mother accused her daughter of lying about her childhood and suggesting she has a mental illness. But it failed to mention that Acton was removed from her mother’s custody at the age of 12 after her stepfather was charged with raping her.

Acton is the first Democrat to become governor of Ohio since 2006. She’s also the first woman ever elected to the office.

entries.title: Sherrod Brown, an Ohio Democrat, wins return to US Senate
entries.summary: More than $500m was spent on the contest, making it one of the most expensive Senate races in US history.
entries.content:
More than $450m was spent on the contest, making it one of the most expensive elections this cycle.

Democrat Sherrod Brown has mounted a successful return to the US Senate, handing a stinging defeat to Republicans who had hoped to hold on to the seat, according to Associated Press news agency projections.

Brown, who was ousted from the Senate two years ago, overcame a costly challenge by incumbent Republican Senator Jon Husted.

More than $500m was spent on advertising in the race, with US tech companies contributing tens of millions to defeat Brown. It was the second most expensive race of this midterm cycle and among the 10 costliest non-presidential races in US history, according to The Hill.

Husted, a strong ally of US President Donald Trump, was appointed to the seat in early 2025 to replace its previous holder, US Vice President JD Vance. He has supported a host of Trump’s second-term policies, including tax cuts, the Iran war and tariffs.

The Ohio race was seen as central in deciding which party controls the Senate. Both of the state’s seats are currently held by Republicans, one of whom helped secure the Senate for Republicans by beating Brown in 2024.

The cost of living was a major issue in the US Midwest, which is home to struggling former industrial cities and rural communities.

Brown championed his strong ties to labour unions and working-class communities in his bid to regain the seat. He will serve the remainder of Vance’s term, which runs until January 2029.

entries.title: Talarico wins Texas Senate race, ending decades of Republican dominance
entries.summary: This is a breaking news story.
entries.content:
James Talarico has won the United States Senate race in Texas, the first time a Democrat has won state office since 1994.

Tuesday’s victory marks a seismic shift in Texas, which has become a standard-bearer for the Republican Party’s staunch conservative policies.

The win comes after a primary intervention by President Donald Trump, which saw him endorse scandal-ridden Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton over Republican Senate candidate John Cornyn.

But Paxton failed to generate enthusiasm, even among his party, despite record-breaking spending, topping more than half a billion dollars.

The largest share came from billionaire donor Elon Musk, who spent at least $212m supporting Paxton.

Musk’s SpaceX company is based in Texas. He has also spent heavily across the country, with Democrats expected to investigate Musk’s role as head of the federal cost-cutting panel DOGE if they take control of Congress.

“It’s historic,” said Taylor Bell, a 27-year-old law student, who attended an election watch party in Houston.

“Hopefully, we see money coming back to the people of Texas, and not more of the same we’ve seen – well, my whole life at this point.”

US Congressman Christian Menefee, a Democrat who represents Houston, told those gathered that “tonight, Texas has restored the hope of a nation”.

“Tonight, I believe firmly that we can accomplish anything in this country if we just stand together and we fight back against hate and bigotry,” he said.

Yvonne Nunga, a 29-year-old who works in IT, said: “The younger generation and all the people who want a better future came out and made their voices heard.

“This party, this fight right now, is not about left or right. It’s about top versus bottom, and I’m so glad that we have candidates that are making this a pivotal point in their messaging,” she added.

“The current politics of the current administration is not working for the people. It’s not for the people, by the people; it’s for the billionaires bought by the billionaires.”

No ‘puppet governor’ for Trump

Tuesday also saw the surprise victory of gubernatorial Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa, whose challenge had been considered a long shot even into the final days of the race.

Hinojosa has become the first Latino governor in the history of Texas, despite Latinos making up 40 percent of the state’s population.

Alejandra Peimbert, a regional communications director for Hinojosa’s campaign, said the victory should be seen as a rebuke to the hardline immigration policies enacted during 10 years under outgoing Governor Greg Abbott.

Abbott has cooperated closely with the Trump administration in its mass deportation campaign, spearheading policies that saw local law enforcement officials conduct immigration enforcement.

“I think the Latino community and our vote has been underestimated by politicians constantly,” Peimbert told Al Jazeera.

“The economy is so bad, and the horrendous things that ICE has done to our community, tearing apart families… I think my community finally had enough,” she added, referring to the Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency.

“President Trump will no longer have a puppet in a governor.”

The state has long been a Republican standard-bearer in the US. But Abbott’s tenure has been defined by a more hardline conservative lurch, with tough approaches not only to immigration, but to social welfare programmes, abortion rights, education and religious freedom.

Abbott’s supporters have touted rapid economic growth in recent years, spurred by tax cuts and regulation rollbacks.

Critics argue that the economic growth measured by these success metrics primarily rewards corporations and the wealthy, while middle- and lower-class Texans see little benefit.

Texas’s poverty rate sits above the national average, with little in the way of social safety nets.

“It’s one of the biggest things Texas can ever experience, because these are two strong candidates that took their time, they took their dedication, and focused with every community in Texas, and so they deserve this position,” said 21-year-old Dylan Sutter about Talarico and Hinojosa.

“Everything is blue. It’s like the ballot itself was painted blue by the time we were done with it.”

entries.title: Democrat Annie Andrews flips South Carolina’s Senate seat
entries.summary: Andrews beats Republican incumbent Darline Graham, sister of the late Senator Lindsey Graham, in a major upset.
entries.content:
In a historic race, Andrews beats Republican incumbent Darline Graham, the sister of late Lindsey Graham.

Charleston, South Carolina, US – South Carolina has elected a Democrat to the US Senate for the first time since 1998, according to the Associated Press news agency. In a major upset for the Republican Party, Annie Andrews won in a state seen as a solid Republican stronghold.

“I think we just made some history,” Andrews said on Tuesday night after results came in.

Andrews outraised Republican candidate Darline Graham by more than $22m, according to Federal Election Commission filings, primarily with grassroots donations. She had pledged to take no money from corporate political action committees (PACs).

Andrews campaigned on lowering costs for working families, expanding affordable healthcare and protecting reproductive rights, and on opposing endless wars.

South Carolina flips

Despite South Carolina being reliably conservative, many voters, including Republicans, believed Graham to be unqualified.

After Republican Senator Lindsey Graham died suddenly in July, his younger sister, Darline, was appointed to serve out the remainder of his term. She went on to win a special primary runoff for the Republican nomination with US President Donald Trump’s endorsement.

Despite Trump’s endorsement, Graham struggled to unite conservatives behind her candidacy. During a primary debate, she said she was “not that informed on national security” and that “national security is not my thing”.

In the final month of the campaign, Trump made multiple appearances alongside Graham, an unusual investment of presidential time in a state Republicans normally win comfortably.

On Tuesday night, Andrews said Graham had called her and congratulated her on her win, which Andrews said she thanked her for.

In a victory speech, Andrews said, “This Senate seat doesn’t belong to one family, one party, or to Washington, DC. It belongs to you and it always will.”

“Nobody in Washington recruited me to run. Nobody handed me a seat in the United States Senate. And nobody wrote me a script,” Andrews said. “I owe no one in Washington anything.”

What does the win mean for South Carolina?

A group of medical students who attend the same medical school as Andrews were celebrating her win at the election watch party. They also volunteer at the free clinic in Mount Pleasant that provides free healthcare to uninsured people.

“Having a scientist in that space means a lot to us,” Daniel Newlands, one of the students, told Al Jazeera.

Lela Ali, a regional voting advisor in the South, told Al Jazeera that Andrews’s win could signal a change not only in South Carolina, but also for southern states.

“I think this victory and the gains across the region today gives people across the South a renewed sense of possibility,” Ali said. “We can’t turn our backs on the South.”
